identity.real_world_identity_notes: The Lamborghini SC63 is an LMDh prototype using the category's common seven-speed Xtrac P1359 hybrid transmission. The base AMS2 identity was live-tested. The exact Low Downforce identity is treated as an aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and has not been separately live-tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, AMS2 1.6.9.91 moved from rest without physical clutch input; the observed launch was hybrid-electric.
Seven paddle-selected forward gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts without driver lift, and automatic cut was perceptible.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with the driver's foot off throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
The exact Lamborghini SC63 - Low Downforce identity inherits these controls as an approved aero-package assumption. Only the base identity was live-tested.
The base configuration was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.

Hybrid move-off, seven paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and a closed GT/Formula display rim were observed directly.
The Low Downforce identity inherits the base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.

The gearbox supplier's own product page, Wikipedia, and Lamborghini's statement that the LMDh gearbox is standardised all agree on seven forward gears, matching the staged observation and the existing curated record. Xtrac's own P1359 product page describes a '7 speed sequential' construction, and Lamborghini confirms this exact gearbox is standard across every LMDh car including the SC63. Neither source states whether gear engagement is by dog rings or synchromesh, so the coarser 'sequential' category is used rather than a specific engagement mechanism, matching the existing curated record's own gearbox_type value. The spec gearbox is paddle-actuated; Lamborghini's own article discusses the steering wheel's paddle-shift controls. All reviewed sources describe a sequential gearbox, matching the staged observation. LMDh/GTP cars use a dashboard button rather than a foot pedal to engage the clutch, per a class-wide technical account; Lamborghini's own article confirms the SC63 uses this identical, standardised LMDh gearbox and clutch system rather than a bespoke one, so there is no driver-operated clutch pedal for standing starts. Matches the existing curated record's finding. driver_summary: The SC63 is Lamborghini's first LMDh prototype, pairing a 3.8-litre twin-turbo V8 developed in-house with the category's standard hybrid gearbox. Iron Lynx raced it from 2024 in WEC and IMSA endurance events.
